I farm this the way I usually do here in Quzhou, starting from what worked for me last year and only adjusting where it makes money. On my land, wheat and summer maize are still the main stomach crops, so I will keep most of the ground in that rotation and leave a smaller block for cauliflower to bring cash. I do have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield instead of gambling on rainfall. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield on 232.9 mu costs more than a bit of extra input, so I will not cut too hard. For wheat, I will keep the base fertilizer solid and then topdress once the seedlings are established and again around jointing if the stand looks strong. For summer maize, I will feed it a bit heavier on nitrogen because if maize goes pale in July, the yield drops fast. For cauliflower, I will spend more per mu because it is a cash crop and needs cleaner management, more water, and tighter pest control. I watch what the capable growers around me do, and around here nobody with good yield goes light on wheat and maize feed when they have well water. I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and improved cauliflower seed, do rotary tillage for the grain land to save time on a large area, and use ploughing on the cauliflower block because that crop responds better when the soil is loosened deeper.
